---
title: "Glossary"
---

AUC (area under the ROC curve)
: The probability that a randomly chosen defaulter is ranked riskier than a randomly chosen
  non-defaulter. 0.5 is a coin toss and 1 is perfect ranking. It measures ranking only, not
  whether the predicted probabilities are right, and it depends on the population it is
  measured on — so these pages never print one without its population.

Booked
: An applicant whose loan was made. The bank observes outcomes only for booked loans; the
  synthetic data give every applicant one, which is how these pages can compare the two
  populations.

EAD (exposure at default)
: The amount owed if the borrower defaults. Pricing here uses the requested amount.

Gate
: A committed minimum a model must meet on held-out data, asserted when it is trained and
  recomputed independently by `verify.py`. A gate is never relaxed to let a model pass; a
  failure is investigated and documented.

Holdout
: The share of the data set aside before fitting and used only to measure the model. A
  held-out metric estimates how the model ranks applicants it has not seen.

IV (information value)
: A single-variable measure of how well a feature separates defaulters from non-defaulters,
  summed over its bins' weights of evidence. Convention reads values below `0.02` as
  unpredictive; IV says nothing about what a feature adds beside the others.

KS (Kolmogorov–Smirnov statistic)
: The largest gap between the cumulative score distributions of defaulters and
  non-defaulters. Like AUC it measures separation, and it too depends on the population.

LGD (loss given default)
: The share of the exposure lost if the borrower defaults, after recoveries. Here it is a
  market assumption in `shared.config.MARKET`, not an estimate.

PD (probability of default)
: The model's estimate that a borrower defaults over the outcome window. The scorecard's PD
  is what every downstream module consumes. The generator's *true* PD is on the leakage
  deny-list: it never exists at decision time.

Proxy
: A feature with no causal role of its own that carries real signal borrowed from one that
  has one — here, columns derived from annual revenue. It ranks, stably and monotonically,
  for someone else's reasons.

PSI (population stability index)
: How far a distribution has moved between two samples, summed over bins. Convention reads
  below `0.10` as stable, `0.10` to `0.25` as worth watching, and above `0.25` as a shift
  that needs action.

RAROC (risk-adjusted return on capital)
: Return after expected loss, divided by the capital held against the risk. Reported by the
  pricing engine beside ROE.

ROE (return on equity)
: Net income on a loan divided by the equity allocated to it. The pricing engine solves for
  the rate at which a loan's ROE meets the hurdle.

Structural zero
: A feature the data generator gives no role in default at all. Any pattern it shows against
  default is sampling noise, however tidy the chart.

VIF (variance inflation factor)
: How much a coefficient's variance is inflated because its feature is predictable from the
  other features. High values mean the model cannot separate those features' effects.

WoE (weight of evidence)
: For one bin of a feature, the log of the ratio of that bin's share of non-defaulters to its
  share of defaulters. A scorecard replaces each raw value with its bin's WoE, so every
  point of the score traces back to one bin of one feature.
